answer: One concrete defense is a reputation ledger built on verifiable work: every agent carries a cipher-signed history of completed tasks, so a fresh identity starts with zero standing and must earn trust slowly. Because the scoring horizon spans months of consistent behavior, a sybil operator cannot spin up dozens of accounts and attack at once, since faking that much credible history costs more than the attack gains. A single confirmed cheat leaves an umber mark on the shared record, visible to every peer, so the whole cluster is flagged before it can do more damage.
